messages:
tom_support: Customer 'neonstream-prod' opened a P0 — embeddings p99 jumped from ~180ms -> ~2.9s after maintenance; they see client retries flooding. repro link: https://traces.redwood/neonstream/9001

rachel_oncall: I'm on it. Region? cluster?

tom_support: ap-south-1 / embed-pool-b. Maintenance window was 01:40-02:05 UTC.

ops-bot: ALERT: ap-south-1 embed route p99 > 2000ms (01:52 UTC). hosts with iowait>8%: 5

ivan_infra: We upgraded NVIDIA driver 535.60 -> 536.23 and kernel 6.1.13 -> 6.1.15 across ap-south-1 during that window. Storage backend also ran thin-provision reclaim sweep at 01:50.

sam_sre: Observing NVMe tail latency on kvcache hosts. fio-ish patterns from kvcache miss load show many small 4k random reads/writes. Example iostat snippet:
```
Device    r/s    w/s   rkB/s wkB/s await %util
nvme0n1  110.0  720.0  4400  28800  42.5  88.1
```

ivan_infra: No NVMe firmware changes. The reclaim sweep is synchronous by default and does lots of tiny IOs.

rachel_oncall: Could io_uring changes in new kernel affect submission queue behavior and increase tail? Worth checking kernel changelog.

sam_sre: Agreed. Quick mitigations: 1) pause reclaim, 2) isolate embed traffic from busy hosts (drain), 3) apply blkio cgroup throttle for reclaim process, 4) bump NVMe device queue_depth and set mq-deadline. I'm going to test (3) and (4) on two canaries.

ivan_infra: Pausing reclaim across ap-south-1 now. Storage notified.

deploy-bot: drain started on ap-s-embed-05/ap-s-embed-11. pods moved: 7/7 each.

sam_sre: To throttle reclaim process using cgroups:
```
echo $$ > /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/reclaim.slice/cgroup.procs
echo "8:0 1048576" > /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/reclaim.slice/blkio.throttle.write_bps_device
```
Applying to reclaim service in containerized job.

sam_sre: Also adjusting NVMe queue on ap-s-embed-05:
```
echo 768 > /sys/block/nvme0n1/device/queue_depth
echo mq-deadline > /sys/block/nvme0n1/queue/scheduler
```

rachel_oncall: Any impact on p99 after canaries?

tom_support: Customer reports fewer retries, partial improvement. Their internal smoke: p99 down to ~650ms for routed tests.

sam_sre: Metrics align — p99 falling on patched/drained hosts. Host iowait trending down. We'll roll in small batches.

ivan_infra: Storage team will add a rate-limiter to reclaim and change it to async batching. ETA ~5h. We'll keep reclaim paused until then.

rachel_oncall: Action items:
- sam: continue rolling cgroup throttle + nvme qdepth changes (2 hosts at a time)
- ivan: keep reclaim paused and coordinate storage rate-limit
- tom: update customer and ask for final smoke after full rollout

deploy-bot: drain completed ap-s-embed-05/ap-s-embed-11. rebalance in flight.

ops-bot: reclaim paused on ap-south-1 at 02:08 UTC.

sam_sre: Note rollback plan: revert qdepth and scheduler and remove cgroup throttle if instability observed; as fallback can roll driver/kernel on a single canary host. We'll document exact commands and thresholds in runbook.

tom_support: Customer final note 03:10 UTC — p99 ~620ms on their test batch, retries minimal. They appreciate the ops help :heart: 

rachel_oncall: Closing pager for now; switching to postmortem. Hypothesis: synchronous thin-provision reclaim burst + blk-mq/io_uring behavior change in kernel/driver -> NVMe qdepth saturation and amplified tail for small-block kv-cache workload. Follow-ups: vendor debug, storage trace correlation, runbook.

sam_sre: I'll author the runbook and PR to ops playbooks repo with detection queries and the quick mitigation steps (pause reclaim, cgroup throttle, nvme tweaks, drains).

ivan_infra: Storage will prototype async reclaim with per-host pacing and a bps cap.

tom_support: last_message_ts: 5042136000 — switching to postmortem thread, will re-open if customer sees regressions.
